capabilities.target: Shared enrichment API account (billed per call)
Researcher sub-agent, which can itself call enrich.lookup and spawn further researchers
CRM account record (industry, size, headquarters fields)

inputs.source: Nightly batch of CRM account rows

instructions.note: The instruction to retry or spawn a researcher and 'keep going until every row is complete' has no stopping condition. Runtime notes state ~3% of the 40,000-row batch has malformed names that never return a complete result, so this instruction guarantees unbounded retries and sub-agent spawning every night absent an external limit.

elements.name: Outbound call to the enrichment API
Shared enrichment API key and monthly quota

controls.name: Per-row and per-batch retry/step cap
controls.decay_rationale: A call/step counter enforced in the orchestration runtime, outside the model, does not weaken as model capability changes.

controls.name: Sub-agent spawn depth and count limit
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the orchestrator that spawns sub-agents, independent of what the model decides.

controls.name: Hard spend cap / circuit breaker on enrich.lookup usage
controls.decay_rationale: A budget enforcement point (API gateway or billing circuit breaker) outside the model halts calls once a threshold is reached, regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Dedicated, isolated API quota for the enrichment agent
controls.decay_rationale: Credential and quota scoping enforced at the API provider does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Spend/budget alert on the enrichment API account
controls.decay_rationale: A monitoring alert outside the model fires on usage thresholds regardless of model behavior; it is detective only and does not itself prevent spend.

controls.name: Prompt instruction to stop after N retries and escalate to a human
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to stop; a more capable or differently tuned model may keep retrying or reason its way past the instruction for rows it judges 'almost complete'.

findings.title: TC6 spend loop: unbounded retries and recursive sub-agent spawning can exhaust the shared enrichment quota (ASI08 cost harvesting / cascading failure)

forecast.watch_signal: Monthly enrichment API spend approaching or exceeding budget without alert; sales or marketing reporting their enrichment/API tools blocked mid-month; nightly batch size or malformed-row rate rising above the current ~3%; median steps or sub-agent spawns per batch rising.

evidence.observation: There is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub agents, and sub agents can spawn their own researchers, so recursion has no structural bound.
enrich.lookup is billed per call, and the API key and its monthly quota are shared with the sales and marketing teams; when the quota runs out, their tools stop working until the next month.

Roughly 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch (about 1,200 rows) have malformed company names that never return a complete result, so the completion condition can never be satisfied for those rows.
The instruction says to retry or spawn a researcher sub agent and 'keep going until every row is complete,' with no stopping condition for rows that structurally cannot complete.
There is no spend alert on the enrichment account, so no detective control would flag abnormal consumption before the shared quota is exhausted.

recommendations.action: Add a hard per-row retry cap and a per-batch call/step cap on enrich.lookup, plus a maximum sub-agent spawn depth and count, all enforced in the orchestration runtime outside the model.
Give the enrichment agent its own API key and quota, isolated from the sales and marketing teams' shared quota, so a runaway here cannot block other teams' tools.

Add a spend/budget alert on the enrichment API account that fires well before the monthly quota is exhausted, and route rows that still fail after the retry cap to a human review queue instead of indefinite retry.
Rewrite the prompt instruction to stop after N retries per row and escalate unresolved rows for human review, instead of 'keep going until every row is complete.'

rating.rationale: The design has no attack path requiring a malicious actor: it has a missing property. Runtime notes state there is no maximum on steps, runtime, retries, or sub-agent spawning, and that sub-agents can recursively spawn further sub-agents. The prompt (prompt.md:2-3) instructs the agent to keep retrying or spawning researchers 'until every row is complete,' but about 3 percent of the 40,000-row nightly batch has malformed company names that can never complete, guaranteeing unbounded retries and spawning every night. enrich.lookup is billed per call and shares its API key and monthly quota with the sales and marketing teams, so this unbounded consumption can exhaust a budget those teams depend on (ASI08 cascading failure / AML.T0034.002 cost harvesting). Per rubric section 5a, the affected capabilities (cap.enrich_lookup and cap.spawn_researcher) are both S3 sinks (spend and delegate actions), the source is internal rather than malicious, so the base tier is the I-row 'high', capped at 'high' because this is a property finding rather than a complete attack path from an untrusted source. No declared control exists anywhere on this path: there is no step cap, spend cap, separate quota, or spend alert, so residual equals the uncredited floor of 'high'. No forecast trigger lowers or changes this, because there are no controls left to decay; the same 'high' persists under longer task horizons or batch growth, which is itself a signal that the gap is structural rather than capability-dependent. The two highest-leverage fixes are a hard, structurally enforced spend/step cap on enrich.lookup and sub-agent spawning, and isolating the enrichment agent's API quota from the shared sales/marketing quota; either would earn rubric step 3 credit and reduce blast radius even without the other.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or billing/alerting configuration was provided; the absence of spend caps, step limits, and alerts is taken as stated in the runtime notes rather than independently verified.

No information was provided about how enrichment API responses are validated before being written to CRM, or about logging and audit trails for agent and sub-agent actions; these areas are marked not_assessed rather than scored.
